key_insight: A 2D DNS/DLM-FD model reproduces the broad hydrodynamic spin-coupling phase behavior of a two-rotor corral, including corotation/counterrotation transitions, but shifts the high-Re reversal boundary relative to experiment.
engineering_relevance: The results help predict how gap size and Reynolds number control passive-rotor spin state in microfluidic or quasi-2D rotor arrays, while highlighting when 3D/end-wall effects may be essential.
method: 2D incompressible viscous-flow DNS using a DLM/FD immersed-boundary style method
Active rotor driven at fixed angular velocity; passive rotor obtained from hydrodynamic torque balance
Phase diagrams computed for multiple corral sizes (C = 3, 4.5, 6) across gap and Reynolds number
evidence_signal: The model matches the benchmark gap-route at Re=20 and captures vortex attachment/detachment/merger, but the predicted high-Re spin boundary differs from experiment and is gap-dependent.
watch_item: Because the model is strictly planar, it may miss finite-depth secondary motion and end-wall shear that likely control the experimental spin reversal.
paper_title: Two-dimensional simulations of hydrodynamic spin coupling in a two-rotor corral
